intro: Professionals and everyday users convert metric tons (t) to kilograms (kg) when working across metric and si standards in engineering specifications, international trade documentation, and technical measurements. One metric ton (tonne / megagram) equals 1,000 kilograms, while 1 kilogram equals 0.001 metric tons. Whether you are verifying mass & weight specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Short Ton (US) vs. Metric Tonne (t) vs. Long Ton (UK)
items: Three distinct units are called a "ton": the US Short Ton equals 2,000 lbs (907.185 kg), the Metric Tonne (t) equals 1,000 kg (2,204.62 lbs), and the British Imperial Long Ton equals 2,240 lbs (1,016.05 kg).
Confusing US short tons with metric tonnes introduces a 10.2% freight weight error on international bills of lading.

faqs.question: How many kilograms (kg) are in 1 metric ton (tonne / megagram) (t)?
faqs.answer: There are 1,000 kilograms (kg) in 1 metric ton (tonne / megagram) (t), which rounds to 1,000 kg for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 kilogram equals 0.001 metric tons.

faqs.question: How do I convert metric tons to kilograms (t to kg)?
faqs.answer: To convert metric tons to kilograms, use the formula: kg = t × 1,000. For example, converting 10 t gives 10,000 kg.

faqs.question: What is 10 metric tons in kilograms?
faqs.answer: 10 metric tons (t) equals exactly 10,000 kilograms (kg) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
